title: Fix crash on closed generic structs from referenced assemblies

lines.text: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).

Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
Members of a type defined in a referenced assembly are reported by the project that defines that type, so an unattributed public member of such a type must be fixed in its defining project.

requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement.intent: A [MessagePackObject] type with a member whose type is a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly must build cleanly and still get a generated resolver.

functional.text: The generator does not throw when a member's type is a closed generic struct or record struct defined in a referenced assembly.
The analyzer does not throw for the same member types.
The compiling assembly gets its generated resolver, as it does when the generic type is declared in the same project.

nonFunctional.text: A failure of the generator or analyzer must not pass silently as a build warning that leaves the assembly without a resolver. (inferred)
Behaviour for generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same project does not change. (inferred)

expectedBehaviours: Compiling a project with a [MessagePackObject] type whose member is a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly (for example a field of type Ref.Pair<int, string>) does not throw IndexOutOfRangeException or any other exception in the source generator.
The same holds when the referenced generic type is a record struct, and when it is used as a property or field.
The build produces no generator-crash warning (CS8785 or similar) for these member types.

No analyzer-crash diagnostic (AD0001) is reported for these member types.
The analyzer reports only the MsgPack diagnostics it would report for an equivalent same-project type, or none.
expectedTests: An analyzer test with a referenced-assembly closed generic struct member finds no AD0001 and no unexpected MsgPack diagnostics.

The generated output matches what is produced when the generic struct is declared in the same project, apart from type location details such as namespaces.

For the reported scenario the build has no crash warning and the resolver exists, so the earlier silent failure is gone.

story.what: The change stops TypeCollector from indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] (and hard-casting the result to PropertyDeclarationSyntax) when it builds the MemberNeedsKey and BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostics. It uses FirstOrDefault and a safe cast instead, so members that exist only in metadata get a null location. It also wraps the analyzer's report callback so a diagnostic is reported only when its location is a syntax tree of the compilation being analyzed. Three new tests compile a generic struct or record struct into a metadata-only assembly, use a closed instance of it as a member, and check that the analyzers and generator report nothing and that the resolver is generated.
story.why: A closed generic struct or record struct from a referenced assembly has no syntax references. The old code threw IndexOutOfRangeException in the generator and the analyzer (seen as CS8785 and AD0001), and the assembly ended up silently without its generated resolver (MP-2283).

claims.text: For a field without a key attribute, the MemberNeedsKey diagnostic location now comes from DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault() instead of [0]. This expression is assigned to a local before any report call, so it runs in both the generator and the analyzer. For a metadata-only field it now yields a null location instead of throwing IndexOutOfRangeException.

findings.title: The code contradicts the description
findings.detail: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation passes a diagnostic on only when its location is in source and in this compilation; all others are dropped. The unkeyed-member test expects the consumer to see no diagnostics at all.
findings.statement: Diagnostics whose location is outside the compilation being analysed are now reported with no location instead of being dropped, so the consuming project still sees them.
